transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (NebulaCare Product), Mark (CTO), Sara (Data Eng), Trevor (ML Eng)

Summary: quick live demo of Redwood Hosted API focusing on embeddings + reranking. Walkthrough included Console snippets, Optimize suggestions for batching/quant, and a short discussion on data residency and SOC2. Customer provided high-level requirements for latency (<150ms p50 on rerank), retention policy, and integration with their on-prem search index.

Topics:
- API endoints: embeddings / reranker
- Model options & cost/latency tradeoffs
- Console: per-route dashboards, token-level cost
- Optimize: batching, prefix cache, quantization recommendations
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC 2, data retention
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we super appreciate it. Um quick intros from our side, Omar and Jonah are with me, they'll run the demo bits.
[00:08] Priya: Hey all, Priya here, Product at NebulaCare. We're excited — we want to tighten our internal KB search, the current recall is noisy.
[00:14] Mark: Mark, CTO. I'm mostly here for the infra questions — latency, egress, and audit logs.
[00:18] Sara: Sara, data eng. I'll be owning ingestion and embedding pipeline.
[00:23] Omar: Great. Quick agenda: show Hosted embeddings endpoint, how to generate vectors, then show how reranker endpoint ties into a retriever+rerank pipeline, then peek at Console and Optimize recs.
[00:32] Trevor: Sounds good. Our key constraints: patient data PII, must be encrypted, retention 30 days for PII-free vectors, and latency p50 for rerank under 150ms.
[00:43] Jonah: Noted. Two quick questions: are you leaning hosted-only or would you want a private deployment?
[00:49] Priya: Ideally hosted due to ease, but we may need VPC peering for compliance.
[00:55] Maya: That's common — hosted + VPC peering is a pattern our customers use. We support a private control plane + VPC connectors. We'll share the network diagram in the packet.
[01:05] Omar: Alright demo start: first the embeddings endpoint. I'm using Python snippets. (typing sounds) We call POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-lite, payload chunk of text. You get back a 768-d vector by default, floats.
[01:22] Mark: Quick q — can we control dim or is model-specific?
[01:26] Omar: Model-specific today, but Optimize recommends lower-dim quant variants for cheaper storage; e.g., redwood-embed-micro is 256-d and we have 8-bit quant profiles.
[01:36] [01:37] (small cross talk)
[01:38] Omar: Now, retrieval pattern: index vectors in your vector DB — we recommend Faiss or Milvus, but we also see customers use managed vector stores. We'll show rerank which runs server-side in Redwood Hosted: send candidate ids + query text to rerank endpoint, it streams back a re-scored list.
[01:54] Trevor: How many candidates do you typically send to reranker?
[01:56] Omar: Usually 50 to 100. For NebulaCare with strict latency, 20-30 is a good starting point. Reranker is a cross-encoder; it's more expensive but much better at precision.
[02:10] Jonah: Demo: calling /v1/rerank with candidates array, you can either send raw text for the top-k or pass ids and we fetch cached passages if you enable prefix KV caching.
[02:22] Priya: What's KV caching? I saw that in the docs but not sure.
[02:26] Omar: KV caching here is prefix or passage caching — K V cache — sorry K V cash — transcription hiccup — basically we cache encoder outputs or passages to avoid re-embedding large docs on each request. Good for static KBs.
[02:39] Mark: Any PII handling? We need masking or redaction hooks before vectors leave our infra.
[02:44] Maya: For hosted, we have optional pre-ingest scrubbing at the SDK layer, and you can run an on-prem preprocess step. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) so data at rest in Redwood is encrypted with your keys.
[02:58] Priya: Great. Also want to understand cost — tokens vs embedding storage.
[03:03] Omar: Cost model: embeddings billed per vector generation, reranker billed per input tokens processed plus a fixed per-call overhead. Optimize can suggest batching windows — e.g., accumulate small user prompts for 100ms to increase batch efficiency while keeping p50 latency under your target.
[03:20] [03:21] (typing / screen share)
[03:22] Omar: Now switching to Console — per-route dashboards. You can see per-request latency distribution, token cost breakdown, and a per-model heatmap. Here's a live demo of a Nebula-like route that is set to model redwood-rerank-large with fallback of redwood-rerank-medium if latency SLOs degrade.
[03:40] Trevor: Can console enforce rollout rules? Eg can we canary 5% of traffic to new rerank model?
[03:44] Jonah: Yes — rollouts and automatic fallback by policy. You can define canary percentages and automatic rollback if p95 latency or error rate crosses thresholds.
[03:54] Mark: About audit logs and traceability — we need fine-grained logs for compliance.
[03:58] Maya: Console exposes request-level traces and an audit log integration for your SIEM; we can forward logs to S3 or your internal log collector with signed delivery.
[04:11] Priya: Let's look at an end-to-end flow: user query -> retriever -> rerank -> top answer.
[04:16] Omar: Yep. For retrieval we recommend using an approximate nearest neighbor store for speed, then a reranker cross-encoder server-side. That reduces false positives. I'll run a sample with 25 candidates from our sample corpus.
[04:27] [04:28] Omar: (runs API call) Results returned in 120ms p50 on my local test with model=redwood-rerank-medium and small batch size.
[04:34] Priya: That's good. Did you enable quantization?
[04:37] Omar: Not on the cross-encoder; quant helps embeddings and encoder models. For reranker we use a mixed precision kernel; Optimize notes recommended: quantize the encoder and keep cross-encoder at fp16 for accuracy.
[04:49] Trevor: If we need sub-100ms, is dedicated better?
[04:52] Omar: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) will give you tighter tail latencies and isolation. For p50 100ms you might need a dedicated pool with optimized batch shape and pinned kernel. Hosted can hit that in many regions but Dedicated is more predictable under load.
[05:06] Mark: Any examples of customers in healthcare?
[05:08] Maya: We have a couple of regulated customers; we can share anonymized performance slides. We'll include a short case study in the follow-up.
[05:17] [05:18] Priya: How does rerank integrate with existing search infra? Our engineers prefer not to refactor the index.
[05:23] Jonah: No refactor needed. Typical pattern: keep your current index for recall, then call Redwood rerank with candidate snippets or ids + your query. We can stream back a score and optionally a highlight.
[05:34] Sara: If we send ids, do you fetch the doc text? That would be a network egress concern.
[05:38] Omar: We fetch if you enable remote doc fetch; otherwise you pass the text. Egress considerations: if you want minimal egress, pass the text in the request from inside your VPC or use the VPC peering pattern so traffic stays inside your network.
[05:52] Mark: Are there rate limits or concurrency limits?
[05:56] Maya: Default limits exist for safety but can be lifted for pilot and prod. For high QPS we recommend Dedicated.
[06:02] [06:03] (typing)
[06:04] Omar: Quick note about Evaluate and Optimize: we run prompt/eval suites against a dev set to watch for regressions after model changes. Optimize will surface quality vs cost tradeoffs and suggest model swaps or quant profiles.
[06:18] Priya: Ok can we do an A/B between redwood-embed-micro+rerank-medium vs redwood-embed-large+rerank-large to measure MRR?
[06:25] Jonah: Absolutely — Console supports A/B test configs and we'll wire up evals to compute MRR on your test corpus.
[06:31] Trevor: For the pilot what's a minimal dataset and time?
[06:35] Maya: We usually recommend 10k passages and 500 queries for an initial pilot (2 weeks). That gives meaningful MRR numbers.
[06:43] Mark: On the compliance docs, can you provide the network diagram and SOC2 attestation?
[06:47] Maya: Yes, will include SOC2 report, ISO sheets, and a network peering diagram in the follow-up packet.
[06:55] [06:56] (brief silence)
[06:57] Omar: Show final Console snippet: here you can set route-specific cost cap, per-request per-caller rate limit, and an automatic fallback to cheaper model when cost threshold exceeded.
[07:14] Priya: Very useful. One more question: can reranker return structured evidence snippets for compliance (e.g., pointer back to original doc + redaction flag)?
[07:22] Jonah: Yes, the rerank response includes doc ids and confidence scores; you can also request redaction metadata if you enable pre-ingest scrubbing.
[07:31] Sara: We'll need the scrub rules documented so our data team can implement them.
[07:35] Maya: We'll add scrub rule examples to the packet.
[07:38] [07:39] (typing)
[07:40] Priya: OK recap and next steps please.
[07:42] Maya: Recap: 1) Hosted embeddings + rerank flow works for your use case. 2) Recommend pilot: 10k passages, 500 queries, 2 weeks; try redwood-embed-micro and redwood-rerank-medium initially. 3) We'll send pricing, SOC2, and a network diagram. 4) Omar will send a notebook with sample rerank calls and optimize settings.
[07:59] Priya: Good, can we lock in pilot start next Monday?
[08:02] Maya: We'll aim to provision trial keys by Friday so you can start next Monday.
[08:06] Mark: Thanks, please include estimated monthly spend for the pilot and for 100k monthly queries.
[08:11] Maya: Noted — will include an estimate.
[08:14] Priya: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[08:17] Maya: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: Some ASR hiccups — KV cache pronounced as K V cash in a couple spots, minor speaker attribution errors around Jonah/Omar overlapping. References shared: /docs/nebulacare/pilot-sow (placeholder), /notebooks/rerank-sample.ipynb (will be uploaded).
